tagline: Break it before users do — test cases, bug hunts, and the automation that keeps releases safe.
what_you_do: You make sure software actually works before it ships. Day to day you write and run test cases, reproduce bugs until you can hand a developer exact steps, do exploratory testing on new features, and re-run regression checks before every release. It's one of the more accessible software rungs: manual QA is self-study viable and doesn't require heavy coding to start. The career, though, grows through automation — Selenium, Playwright, Cypress — and toward SDET, where testing becomes an engineering discipline of its own.
day_in_life: Run the regression checklist against last night's build and log anything that broke
Reproduce a customer-reported bug until you can write exact steps a developer can follow
Exploratory-test a new feature, probing edge cases the requirements never mentioned
Write and update test cases as the sprint's stories change underneath you
Flag a release risk in standup that nobody else has noticed yet

salary.entry: ~$55,000–$70,000 to start (manual QA — industry figure, not BLS)
salary.growth: +15% — counted in the same fast-growing group as software developers
salary.note: U.S. BLS figure for Software Quality Assurance Analysts and Testers (15-1253); a median is the midpoint of everyone employed, so entry pay runs lower — the entry range here is an industry estimate, not BLS. Verify against the live BLS page before deciding.

downsides: QA is often treated as lower-status than development, and pay lags dev until you automate. Release weeks bring crunch, regression testing is genuinely repetitive, and there's steady pressure to move from manual testing into automation faster than you may feel ready for.

fits_if: You instinctively poke at things to see how they break
You like methodical, checklist-driven work with visible results
You want a software career without starting from heavy coding
less_ideal_if: You need to build features to feel satisfied — finding flaws in others' work grates on some people
You'd rather avoid delivering critical feedback, sprint after sprint

skills.name: Testing fundamentals (test cases, test plans, coverage)
skills.note: How to turn 'does it work?' into a repeatable, reviewable process.

skills.name: Bug reporting & reproduction
skills.note: Exact steps, expected vs. actual, environment — a great bug report is your calling card.

skills.name: SQL & API testing basics
skills.note: Check the data behind the screen; poke APIs with Postman.

skills.name: Test automation (Selenium / Playwright / Cypress)
skills.note: The skill that moves you from tester to engineer — and raises pay.

skills.name: Programming (JavaScript / Python / Java)
skills.note: The SDET track — building full automation frameworks — runs on real code.

certs.title: ISTQB Certified Tester Foundation Level
certs.reason: The one QA credential hiring managers recognize worldwide — lifetime validity, and it formalizes the vocabulary of the craft.

cert_note: Honest priority check: a public portfolio of real test plans, sharp bug reports, and one small automation project beats any QA cert on a resume. ISTQB CTFL is an optional filter-passer, not a requirement.

trial.objective: Do the actual job for an evening: pick a public website, try to break it methodically, and write up what you find as professional bug reports.
trial.disclosure: Just a browser and a text editor — everything stays on your machine, submit nothing, contact no one. You're practicing the write-up, not reporting real bugs.

roadmap.title: Learn how testing works
roadmap.focus: Test-case design, the bug lifecycle, and where QA sits in the software process — free via Test Automation University and Ministry of Testing. Practice on demo apps built to be tested.

roadmap.title: Build a public portfolio
roadmap.focus: Write real test plans and bug reports against open-source or practice apps and put them on GitHub. This is your resume — manual QA hiring runs on demonstrated craft, not credentials. Add ISTQB CTFL if listings in your market ask for it.

roadmap.title: Land manual QA and learn the product
roadmap.focus: Get in as a tester, master the domain, and quietly add SQL and API testing (Postman) — the skills that separate you from checklist-only testers.

roadmap.title: Automate
roadmap.focus: Pick Playwright or Cypress, learn enough JavaScript or Python to be dangerous, and automate your own team's most repetitive regression checks. Pay and status both move here.

roadmap.title: Grow toward SDET
roadmap.focus: Build test frameworks, wire tests into CI/CD, and own quality as an engineering problem — or use the coding base to branch into development outright.

adjacent_paths.reason: Automation skills turn QA into SDET and open the dev door.
QA discipline and requirements-thinking transfer directly into coordination and BA work.
